entries.clue: Financially reliable American making a bit of money once (7)

blocks.note: a solid firm is financially sound

annotation.surface: A dependable American banker earns a little cash.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks the coin as historical: the solidus was a gold coin of the late Roman Empire.
annotation.definitionFit: The solidus was a Roman coin, so a bit of money from long ago.

entries.clue: English arts graduate following reduced school form (6)

indicators.note: SCHOOL is cut down to its short form SCH
to follow is to come after, so E and MA are placed after SCH

blocks.note: SCH is the standard abbreviation of school

annotation.surface: An English graduate comes after a pupil from a shrunken school year.
annotation.walkthrough: 'School form' reads as one phrase, a class in a school; split it, and 'form' is the definition, meaning an outline or pattern.
annotation.definitionFit: A schema is a plan or outline, a form in the abstract sense.

entries.clue: Drink in the course of duty, showing lack of seriousness (6)

indicators.note: the drink sits during, so inside, the duty

blocks.note: a levy is a tax or duty
IT is Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

annotation.surface: Someone drinking while on duty isn't taking the job seriously.
annotation.walkthrough: LEV(IT)Y. 'Duty' looks like work, but here it is a tax.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: frivolity or flippancy where gravity is called for.

entries.clue: Show lack of respect for accolade in broadcast (10)

blocks.note: to dis someone is to disrespect them

annotation.surface: Someone sneers at an award during a television programme.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks like a TV noun, but it is the verb meaning to scatter widely, as seed is broadcast.
annotation.definitionFit: To broadcast is to spread widely, which is to distribute.

entries.clue: Point in the deep provided with barriers (5)

indicators.note: a point in the deep is located within it, so PT sits inside SEA

blocks.note: PT is the abbreviation of point

annotation.surface: A spot out in the ocean has been fenced off.
annotation.walkthrough: SE(PT)A. Septa are dividing walls, as in the nasal septum, a Latin plural.
annotation.definitionFit: Septa are partitions in the body or a plant, barriers between compartments.

entries.clue: Female getting well and truly overtaken panicked (7)

blocks.note: a runner lapped has been passed by a whole lap

annotation.surface: A woman who is left far behind in a race loses her cool.
annotation.walkthrough: To flap is to get in a panic, as in 'don't flap'.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal British sense: to be in a flap, flustered and agitated, is to panic.

entries.clue: Become dim about Trump’s country having bad discharge of weaponry (9)

indicators.note: about means around, so FADE is wrapped around what follows

blocks.note: to fade is to grow dim
ill = bad, as in ill will

annotation.surface: Someone losing their wits over American politics goes off like a gun.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Having' is the link that lets the definition follow the wordplay; 'discharge' looks medical after 'bad', but it is gunfire.
annotation.definitionFit: A fusillade is a burst of simultaneous gunfire.

entries.clue: Very eager to get a medal (not new) (4)

indicators.note: the medal is taken without anything new, so its N (new) goes

blocks.note: GONG, slang for a medal, without its N

annotation.surface: Someone can't wait to win a medal.
annotation.walkthrough: GONG is British slang for a medal or honour, and N = new.
annotation.definitionFit: Agog means eagerly excited.

entries.clue: Map out what sounds like zone for flatworms (8)

indicators.note: tells you to use a word that is said like AREA

blocks.note: to plan is to map out
a zone is an area, which is said like ARIA

annotation.surface: A zoologist charts the territory of flatworms.
annotation.walkthrough: Planaria are a genus of freshwater flatworms.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: planaria is a genus name, used loosely for the whole group of freshwater flatworms.

entries.clue: Fighter suitable, left on register (8)

indicators.note: L is put on, before, LIST

blocks.note: due = fitting, as in due respect

annotation.surface: A suitable fighter's name is left on the roll.
annotation.walkthrough: The double L is easy to miss: one from DUE-L and one starting LIST.
annotation.definitionFit: A broad term for a narrow one: any fighter, narrowed to one who fights formal one-to-one duels.

entries.clue: Eruption in bees’ homes (5)

definitions.note: 'Eruption' is singular; HIVES is a single rash despite the plural form

blocks.note: a skin eruption, an itchy rash
where a colony of bees lives

annotation.surface: Something bursts out inside a beehive.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eruption' suggests a volcano; here it is a skin eruption, the rash called hives.
annotation.definitionFit: Hives, or urticaria, is an eruption of itchy welts on the skin.

entries.clue: The old man’s account about soldiers in musical composition (9)

indicators.note: the account wraps around the soldiers

blocks.note: PA = the old man, father; PA'S

annotation.surface: Dad's war story gets set to music.
annotation.walkthrough: PAS + T(OR)ALE. 'The old man' is slang for one's father.
annotation.definitionFit: A pastorale is a musical piece evoking country life.

entries.clue: Mum and I join forces to a significant extent (10)

blocks.note: mater is Latin for mother, old public-school slang for mum
to ally is to join forces

annotation.surface: A mother and child team up in a big way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mum' more usually gives MA; here it is the longer MATER.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something that matters materially matters substantially, in a way that makes a real difference.

entries.clue: Old deity, trite, heartless (4)

indicators.note: the middle letter, the heart, is removed

annotation.surface: A god of old dismissed as cliched and unfeeling.
annotation.walkthrough: BA(N)AL minus its heart. Baal was a Canaanite god in the Old Testament.
annotation.definitionFit: Baal was an ancient Semitic god.

entries.clue: Like some plants Greek character hadn’t given up consuming (10)

blocks.note: still = continuing, not having given up

annotation.surface: A Greek who refused to quit dieting eats like a herbivore.
annotation.walkthrough: A pistillate flower has pistils, the female parts, but no stamens.
annotation.definitionFit: Pistillate describes plants or flowers bearing pistils only.

entries.clue: One facing restrictions behind bars for heinous acts (11)

indicators.note: I stands in front of TIES
I and TIES come after BARBAR

annotation.surface: A prisoner locked up for terrible crimes.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a convict behind bars; the wordplay takes 'bars' literally, as two BARs.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a barbarity is a savagely cruel act, as heinous as acts come.

entries.clue: Wicked ruler said to be living out in the country? (9)

indicators.note: treats the letters as bad, so rearranged

annotation.surface: A tyrant is reported to be retiring to the countryside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Said' looks like a homophone signal, but it is just fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Ruralised means made rural, settled into country life.

entries.clue: Somerset’s original eatery with ancient wooden platform? (8)

indicators.note: take the first letter of Somerset
with means accompanied by, so OLD is added on after S and CAFF

blocks.note: caff is British slang for a cheap cafe

annotation.surface: A Somerset cafe has an old wooden stage outside.
annotation.walkthrough: Somerset is an English county. The question mark admits a scaffold is only sometimes wood.
annotation.definitionFit: A scaffold is a raised platform, of wood for gallows or builders.

entries.clue: Supposed to have set musical show up (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, up reverses the word

blocks.note: to set something down is to put it

annotation.surface: Someone was meant to stage a musical.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set' and 'show up' look like theatre business; the musical is EVITA, flipped.
annotation.definitionFit: Putative means commonly supposed or reputed.

entries.clue: Fake matter surprisingly free, having a certain appeal (11)

indicators.note: FREE is rearranged in a surprising way

blocks.note: IT = sex appeal, as in the It girl

annotation.surface: A forged item is oddly free yet has a certain charm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Matter' looks like a noun, stuff; it is the verb, to count.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a counterfeit note or painting is a fake one.

entries.clue: Character carrying an untrue report (6)

indicators.note: to carry is to hold, so CARD holds AN within it

blocks.note: a card is an eccentric character

annotation.surface: A colourful figure spreads a false story.
annotation.walkthrough: CA(N A)RD. A 'card' is an amusing, eccentric person.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowing from French, where canard means duck; in English it is a hoax or baseless rumour.

entries.clue: Make severe demands on family (6)

blocks.note: to overtax, push something beyond its limit
a breed or line of descent

annotation.surface: Relatives place heavy demands on one another.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On family' reads as one phrase; it splits between the two definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: Strain means both to overtax and a lineage or stock.

entries.clue: Pastry item – maybe attendee at football match has devoured fifty (4)

indicators.note: what is devoured ends up inside the eater, so L goes inside FAN

blocks.note: a fan at a match, one example

annotation.surface: A football supporter wolfs down fifty pies.
annotation.walkthrough: F(L)AN. 'Maybe' flags FAN as one example of a match attendee.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a flan, an open tart in a pastry case, is one item a baker makes from pastry.

entries.clue: Manifestly immoral measure not right for suffering penitent? (10)

indicators.note: the measure goes in, not the R

blocks.note: an ell is an old measure of length
R = right; ELL replaces it: FLAG(R→ELL)ANT

annotation.surface: A sinner mortifies himself with harsh measures.
annotation.walkthrough: FLAG(R)ANT with ELL taking the R's place. The question mark: a flagellant whips himself as penance.
annotation.definitionFit: A flagellant is a penitent who scourges himself.

entries.clue: Teased escort audibly (5)

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so take a word that sounds like the escort word

blocks.note: to escort is to guide; the past tense is what is heard

annotation.surface: A chaperone was mocked out loud.
annotation.walkthrough: To guy someone is to ridicule them, from Guy Fawkes effigies.
annotation.definitionFit: Guyed means made fun of, ridiculed.

entries.clue: Signs of displeasure – no time for increase in confidence? (4)

indicators.note: 'no time' means leaving out the time, so T is dropped

annotation.surface: Jeers leave no chance for someone's morale to recover.
annotation.walkthrough: BOOS(T). The question mark: a boost need not be to confidence.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a crowd shows its displeasure by booing, the plural covering the jeers.

entries.clue: I’m US loony, going wild menacingly (9)

indicators.note: the letters run wild, rearranging

annotation.surface: A self-declared American madman goes on a threatening rampage.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in I'm is ignored; all nine letters are used.
annotation.definitionFit: Ominously means in a threatening, menacing way.

entries.clue: Lizard rescuers in vehicles found outside school (5)

indicators.note: the rescuers are found on the outside, so AA wraps around GAM

blocks.note: the AA, Automobile Association, rescues broken-down cars in Britain
a gam is a school of whales

annotation.surface: Lifeguards in cars spot a lizard near a school.
annotation.walkthrough: A(GAM)A. The AA is Britain's roadside breakdown service; a gam is a school of whales, not a classroom.
annotation.definitionFit: A specific for the general: agamas are a family of Old World lizards, often brightly coloured.

entries.clue: Spiced up in a miniskirt. say (7)

blocks.note: of food, given a sauce or seasoning, as a salad is
wearing clothes, a miniskirt being one example

annotation.surface: Someone livened up their look with a miniskirt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spiced up' suggests racy clothing, but it is food: dressed crab, dressed salad.
annotation.definitionFit: Dressed means seasoned (of food) and clothed.

entries.clue: City river penetrating some foreign hideout (7)

indicators.note: to penetrate is to go into, so R enters DES

annotation.surface: A river runs through a hidden lair abroad.
annotation.walkthrough: D(R)ES + DEN. Dresden is a city in eastern Germany.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Dresden, capital of Saxony, is one example of a city.
